stories.title: Attacks and blockade enforcement around Hormuz
stories.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued into November. Today's trade press reports a tanker confirmed struck in the Gulf, with Iran claiming two tankers hit mines and a VLCC sunk.
stories.why_it_matters: Hull strikes and crew-safety concerns raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings and shrink the pool of willing owners; depressed transit volumes reshape crude and product ton-miles.
stories.latest: A tanker was confirmed struck in the Gulf and Iran claims a VLCC sinking and two tankers hit by mines. Separately, Fujairah VLSFO rose $34.00 (+4.1%) to $856.50/t today, though the data does not establish a link.
sources: Tanker confirmed struck in the Gulf, Iran claims VLCC sinking

stories.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea and Baltic
stories.what: Drone strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea have intensified. Three commercial vessels were struck near Romania's Sulina anchorage, prompting Romanian fighter jets to scramble and protests from Bucharest, while a freighter damaged in an earlier Russian drone strike is drifting toward Bulgarian waters.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling in the region; proximity to NATO territory widens the risk area.
stories.latest: Three more ships hit by drones off Romania, fighter jets scrambled, and an abandoned damaged freighter drifting south toward Bulgaria.
sources: Black Sea drone attacks trigger Romanian fighter jet scramble
Three More Ships Hit by Drone Strikes off Coast of Romania
Abandoned Freighter Drifts Towards Bulgarian Waters

stories.title: US Jones Act waiver extended again
stories.what: President Trump is extending the waiver allowing energy companies and traders to move oil, fertilizer and other commodities between US ports on foreign-flagged ships for another 90 days. The pause has now stretched past 230 days.
stories.why_it_matters: The waiver keeps foreign-flag tonnage eligible for US coastwise cargoes, affecting demand for US-flag ships and the employment of product tankers in domestic trades.

stories.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
stories.what: US sanctions have expanded across Cuban maritime entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks, while the dark fleet is described as a parallel fleet that has tripled since 2022. The US Treasury may now allow companies to buy sanctioned vessels and return them to legitimate trade case by case.
stories.why_it_matters: Registry fraud and designations force charterers and insurers to re-verify documents and positions; a licensing route back to legitimate trade could return tonnage to the compliant fleet.

stories.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
stories.what: A reported US-Russia arrangement on extra diesel for the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a ban on most diesel exports to end-January.
stories.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment.

stories.title: US port fees on Chinese-built and Chinese-operated ships
stories.what: The US administration has formally extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue.
stories.why_it_matters: The fees, if reinstated, would change the cost of deploying Chinese-built tonnage into US trades and affect chartering preferences across sectors.
